title: y-cases — accessibility cases anchored to screens.json, with candidates and dismissals kept

rows.description: A ceiling and deliberately no floor, for the reason stated in themes/schema.json: a minimum tells a collector to reach a number. Fifteen confirmed cases with their dismissals beside them are worth more than twenty-five that were reached for.

counts.description: additionalProperties is false here to do a job the prose cannot: there is no lawful place to put by_source or by_country. Most of this corpus is national government portals, and a per-source tally is a ranking of governments wearing a teaching dataset's clothes.

by_failure_type.description: The brief caps any one type at five. JSON Schema cannot express that against a computed tally, so it is a hand check.

screens_covered.description: Distinct screen_id values. The brief asks for at least twelve, and for no more than two cases from any one screen.

detector.description: The rule engine that raised the candidates. A case found by a tool is only reproducible if the tool is named and versioned.

hand_checks.description: The three rules the schema cannot enforce — that every screen_id resolves, that no failure_type exceeds five, that no screen carries more than two cases. Recording who checked and when makes the gap auditable instead of merely known.

screen_id.description: Must be an id that already exists in screens.json. The shape is checkable here; the existence is not, which is why this dataset is blocked on that one rather than merely ordered after it.

wcag_ref.description: Null is common and correct. Plenty of real failures breach no success criterion, and recording one that does not apply is worse than recording none.

measurement.description: Present only where evidence is measured, and null everywhere else. A number nobody took is the shape of the fabrication this folder is designed against.

status.description: A candidate is a tool's output and is never taught as a failure. Dismissed cases are kept: a real flag dismissed for a stated reason on a named screen is the most useful record in the file.

dismissed_because.description: State which exception applies — the inline exception in SC 2.5.8, the two-dimensional exception in SC 1.4.10, incidental text in SC 1.4.3.

what_the_user_hits.description: The consequence for a person, in one sentence. Not the criterion restated: 'the focus ring is invisible against the blue header' rather than 'fails SC 2.4.7'.

then.description: measured requires the number that was taken.
If nobody measured it, the field is null rather than estimated.
A person turns a candidate into a case, and the file records which person.
A dismissal without a reason is a deletion with extra steps.
